# What to Know About Ted Turner's 3 Ex-Wives, Including Actress Jane Fonda

Ted Turner was most famously married to actress Jane Fonda for 10 years

By

[Samantha Stutsman]

### NEED TO KNOW

* CNN founder Ted Turner was married three times to Julia Nye, Jane Shirley Smith and actress Jane Fonda
* He welcomed two children with Nye and three children with Smith
* Turner died on May 6 at age 87

[Ted Turner], who died at age 87 on May 6, was married three times during his life.

The CNN founder wed Julia Gale Nye in 1960. The couple went on to welcome [two children], daughter Laura and son Robert "Teddy" Edward IV,before divorcing after just a few years of marriage.

In 1964, Turner married Jane Shirley Smith. The pair, who eventually split in 1988, welcomed three children, Beau, Rhett and Jennie.

The media mogul's final marriage was to actress [Jane Fonda] from 1991 to 2001. During an [interview] with [Piers Morgan] in 2012, Turner admitted that Fonda was "probably" the great love of his life.

"When you love somebody, and you really love them, you never stop loving them," the media mogul added. "There's nothing wrong with that. That's good."

Here's everything to know about Ted Turner's ex-wives: Julia Gale Nye, Jane Shirley Smith and Jane Fonda.

## Julia Gale Nye

![Image 5: Ted Turner.]:max_bytes(150000):strip_icc():focal(748x368:750x370):format(webp)/ted-turner-portrait-050626-277890d77347498b98e1ddfea9ef2406.jpg)

Ted Turner.
Bettmann/Getty

Julia Gale Nye, the daughter of world champion sailor Harry Gale Nye Jr., met Ted Turner while he was attending Brown University in 1959. The couple married at St. Chrysostom’s Episcopal Church in Chicago on June 22, 1960, according to the [_Chicago Tribune_].

They later welcomed a daughter, Laura, in 1961, and a son, Robert Edward IV, in 1963, before going their separate ways, per Michael O'Connor's book _Ted Turner: A Biography_.

## Jane Shirley Smith

![Image 9: Ted Turner attends official CNN Launch event on June 01, 1980 in Atlanta, Georgia.]:max_bytes(150000):strip_icc():focal(784x129:786x131):format(webp)/ted-turner-cnn-launch-event-050626-bc5f511d705c4cc98766d1019fa4f72e.jpg)

Ted Turner attends official CNN Launch event on June 01, 1980 in Atlanta, Georgia.
Rick Diamond/Getty

Shortly after his divorce from Nye, Turner married Jane Shirley Smith on June 2, 1964. Smith, a Delta Air Lines flight attendant, reportedly [met Turner at a Young Republicans meeting].

The couple welcomed three children together: son Rhett in 1965 — named after Rhett Butler from _Gone with the Wind_ — followed by son Beau in 1968 and daughter Sarah Jean “Jennie” in 1969.

Turner and Smith divorced in 1988.

## Jane Fonda

![Image 11: Jane Fonda and Ted Turner attend the Volunteers of America's First Annual Glasnost Awards on March 22, 1990 in Beverly Hills, California.]:max_bytes(150000):strip_icc():focal(999x0:1001x2):format(webp)/jane-fonda-ted-turner-b9dbb729dcef407facfc7aa4e86a297e.jpg)

Jane Fonda and Ted Turner attend the Volunteers of America's First Annual Glasnost Awards on March 22, 1990 in Beverly Hills, California.Ron Galella, Ltd./Ron Galella Collection/Getty

Turner and Jane Fonda began dating in 1990, shortly after she split from her second husband, Tom Hayden. The couple [married on Dec. 21, 1991] — Fonda’s 54th birthday — at Turner’s 8,100-acre plantation, Avalon, in Capps, Fla.

“[With Ted] there were lovemaking times when we'd lock eyes and melt into one," she wrote in her 2005 memoir, _My Life So Far_. "There were times when something would set us to laughing so hard we'd sink to the floor, like the night when our guffaws collapsed us at the foot of the Gone With the Wind staircase at his plantation, and we had to crawl up to bed on hands and knees.”

After their wedding, Fonda stepped away from acting and focused on married life with Turner. But over time, cracks began to form in their relationship as the pair struggled with differing needs and lifestyles. They separated in 2000 and finalized their divorce the following year.

"He needs someone to be there one hundred percent of the time,” Fonda told [_The New Yorker_] in 2001. “He thinks that’s love. It is not love. It’s babysitting. We went in different directions. I grew up.”

Still, Fonda continued to speak warmly about their relationship in the years since their divorce, even calling him her "favorite ex-husband."

"I had a great time for 10 years. I am just so happy that I got to spend 10 years with him," she told Piers Morgan in 2012.
